editorial.headline: Cleaning as an Operating Discipline
editorial.standfirst: A broad cleaning activity, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally, with no Bali PMA moratorium block at the Large scale.
editorial.body:
This activity is the working backbone behind clean, maintained and usable premises. Its scope runs well beyond routine interiors: it includes exterior cleaning for buildings ranging from offices and factories to shops, institutions, professional premises and multi-unit residences. It also reaches specialist work on windows, chimneys, fireplaces, stoves, incinerators, boilers, ventilation ducts and gas or vapour exhausts. The common thread is practical upkeep of the built environment, whether the task is visible from the street or buried inside a building’s systems.

The range is deliberately broad. Pool cleaning and maintenance sit alongside industrial-machine cleaning, bottle washing, and cleaning for trains, buses and aircraft. It also includes the interiors of ships and tanker trucks, street cleaning, snow and ice removal, post-construction building cleaning, and exterior work performed with steam, sand blasting or similar methods. Residential vector, disease-carrying animal and pest control is within scope too, including delivery in buildings, settlements, industrial sites and other business premises, as well as at airports, ports and land-border crossings.

The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is a clear national position: foreign investment is not limited to a minority holding for this activity. The source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not add a moratorium block to this activity’s PMA registration. The province’s standing rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as Medium-High/High, so the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The practical reading is precise rather than promotional: the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the national benchmark, while Bali’s recorded position is that this activity is not stopped by the provincial moratorium at the Large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: Cleaning is treated here as a broad operating discipline, not a narrow housekeeping service.
